project: Shadow (Rust MoE inference engine, repo J:\Shadow on this PC)
task: Bench prompt-side speculation - the one speed lever that multiplies and has never been measured.
state_of_the_tree: Uncommitted work in progress: the UI fix (raw-XML strip + collapsible cards on reopen, in CHANGELOG) and quant-kernel work in engine.rs (matvec/mma Q4_K/Q5_K, SHADOW_MMA_QK, SHADOW_DELTA_X8). Build on top of it, do not revert it.
the_unprobed_asymmetry: Speculation on DECODE is measured and kept (--spec 3, DFlash 2 accepted, 52.1 tok/s vs Strata's 47.7). Speculation on PROMPTS has never been benched. A prompt pass is one big batch; if the draft accepts even two tokens on a long prompt, that pass's expert traffic amortizes over 3x the tokens - the DRAM cost per token DROPS instead of rising. Decode acceptance is 0.55-0.95; on a cold prompt the first token's router tops are exactly the ones the cache hasn't seen, so the draft must be right about those - the same bet the cache admission filter already makes and wins.
why_this_is_the_one_to_run: It is the cheapest experiment on the list: no new code, just arms. If it wins it multiplies the copy path's payoff too, because every accepted token is a token that didn't pay for its own expert.
bench_arms: arm A: baseline, spec off, prompt-heavy workload
arm C: baseline, mixed prompt+decode (the usual headline)
4 arms x 3 runs, interleaved, one fresh launch per run, warm turns only
scoring: TOTAL throughput, not the median. Noise floor 0.8% median / 2.0% p90 - anything under ~1% is a tie, and a tie is a loss.
harness: bench/bench_total.py and bench_vs_strata.ps1 are the scoring harnesses; bench/*.sh (fid, corr, ceil, chunk, mb, post) are the existing workload scripts; the prompt-2026-11-02-b2k-cross-session* dirs are the last prompt benchmarks - match their shape. tools/autotune.py is the tuning loop.

machine_facts.gpu: RTX 5070 12.2 GB, expert cache 4.42 GiB (bigger caches measured as losses: 4.8 -5%, 5.0 -10%)
machine_facts.cpu: i7-11700K, 8C/16T, HAS full AVX-512 (verified via CPUID family 6 model 167)
machine_facts.dram: DDR4-2933 ~30 GB/s - the wall; copy engine gets 13, link can do 23-28
machine_facts.ram: 64 GB, 36 GiB pinned tier, 3 GiB pinned floor (machine froze hard at 0.4 GiB free)
machine_facts.model: 89 GiB IQ3_S GGUF, mmap'd from disk; OS file cache ~50 GiB, buffered reads ~9.5 GB/s, unbuffered 3.5 GB/s (drive ceiling)

rules: measure, and what loses stays opt-in (off by default)
every experiment gets a dated STATUS.md entry with its measured numbers, wins and losses alike
do not touch the decode path (it is already a win: 52.1 vs Strata's 47.7)
do not change the pinned tier, the floor, or the cache size
the flag-level knobs are exhausted - the tuning loop said so when it stopped; this is a bench, not a tuning run
expected_cost: no new code; ~40 min per bench round + server restarts (36 s load, ~30 s tier refill)
honest_odds: about 50/50. The asymmetry is real and unprobed; the risk is that prompt-side acceptance is lower than decode-side (cold router tops), and the draft's cost - which ate most of the decode gain - is paid per-pass, not per-token, so a low acceptance rate on prompts is worse than on decode.
second_lever_still_pending: The Avalon port (move compute to the data: CPU computes cache-miss experts straight from the mmap'd file, one DRAM read, no host join) is unbuilt - its spec is docs/EXPERIMENT_SPEC_2026-11-01.json, ~40% odds, same DRAM math, kernel already fast enough at 17-21 GB/s. Run this bench first; it's cheaper, and if it wins the Avalon port's payoff multiplies too.
